content.text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is an O–P(=S)(OCH3)2 group, a dimethyl thiophosphate ester. The other is a sulfonamide, S(=O)(=O)NH2.

Reading the pieces:
- Phosphorus carries a double bond to S, two OCH3 groups, and an O that links to the ring.
- The ring is drawn as a benzene with alternating double bonds.
- The sulfur on the ring carries two double-bonded O atoms and an NH2.

SMILES: COP(=S)(OC)Oc1ccc(cc1)S(N)(=O)=O
